name: env
description: Runs a command with a modified environment, or prints the current environment.

flags.description: Run CMD with an extra/overridden variable.
Run with an EMPTY environment (isolation testing).

examples.explanation: All environment variables, sorted and paged — how you discover what a program can see.
Runs the app with NODE_ENV set for this invocation only — nothing leaks into your shell.
Starts bash with an empty environment — the classic "why does it work for me but not in cron?" reproducer.

about: env is an external binary, which makes it usable in shebangs: #!/usr/bin/env python3 finds python3 via PATH regardless of its location — the portable shebang. The cron environment problem is the top use case for env -i debugging: cron runs with a minimal environment unlike your shell.
useCases: Run commands with temporary variable overrides.
Debug "works in shell, fails in cron" issues.
mistakes: Assuming cron has your shell environment — it does not; define what you need in the crontab or a wrapper.
